title: Left adjoints preserve locally surjective families of sheaves
statement: Let C and D be categories in arbitrary independent object and morphism universes, with Grothendieck topologies J and K. Fix a value universe w, and let L:Sh(J,Type w)→Sh(K,Type w) be left adjoint to G. Let (f_i:A_i→B) be any set-indexed family of sheaf maps. Suppose that for every section x of B over U there is a J-covering sieve S of U such that for every arrow a:V→U in S some section y of some A_i(V) maps to the restriction of x. Then the family (L(f_i):L(A_i)→L(B)) satisfies the same local-surjectivity condition on K. No relation between the index, value, or site universes is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00WL, Lemmas 7.11.2–3; adjunction and local image argument

proof.text: A locally surjective family jointly lifts against a monomorphism. Pull back the monomorphism along the proposed map from B. The projection is mono and is locally surjective by the family condition, hence an isomorphism by the local bijectivity criterion.

Take the subfunctor of L(B) that is the union of the images of L(f_i), then its locally generated subsheaf. Its inclusion is mono and each L(f_i) factors through it. Transpose these factorizations along the adjunction. The right adjoint preserves monomorphisms, so joint lifting factors the unit B→G(L(B)) through the direct image of this inclusion.

Transpose back to obtain a retraction of the subsheaf inclusion. Every section of L(B) therefore lies in the locally generated union of images. The defining covering sieve of subfunctor sheafification is the desired local-surjectivity sieve. This also covers an empty family.

lean.statement:
theorem map_jointly_locally_surjective
    {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D] {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    (L : Sheaf J (Type w) ⥤ Sheaf K (Type w))
    (G : Sheaf K (Type w) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type w)) (adj : L ⊣ G)
    {ι : Type*} {A : ι → Sheaf J (Type w)} {B : Sheaf J (Type w)}
    (f : ∀ i, A i ⟶ B)
    (hf : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : B.obj.obj U),
      ∃ S : Sieve U.unop, S ∈ J U.unop ∧
        ∀ (V : C) (a : V ⟶ U.unop), S a →
          ∃ (i : ι) (y : (A i).obj.obj (op V)),
            (f i).hom.app (op V) y = B.obj.map a.op x) :
    ∀ (U : Dᵒᵖ) (x : (L.obj B).obj.obj U),
      ∃ S : Sieve U.unop, S ∈ K U.unop ∧
        ∀ (V : D) (a : V ⟶ U.unop), S a →
          ∃ (i : ι) (y : (L.obj (A i)).obj.obj (op V)),
            (L.map (f i)).hom.app (op V) y = (L.obj B).obj.map a.op x
